incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: SVC-SYNTH-DB-LATENCY in prod-us-east-1. Synthetic check 'canary-db-conn' reporting 90th percentile DB connect latency > 500ms for 3 consecutive minutes. Link: https://mon.redwood.local/alerts/SVC-SYNTH-DB-LATENCY
pd-bot: PagerDuty notification: Incident INC-12345 created and routed to oncall. Escalation level: P1.
Alex (oncall): ack — I'm taking this. Pinging infra and SRE. Any obvious customer reports yet?
Leah (sre): seeing a bump in 5xx traces on api-ingest between 10:42-10:47 UTC. Error rate ~2x normal. No major traffic drop.
Sanjay (infra): running quick checks on DB layer + hosts. Preliminary: one replica with high IO wait.
Maya (prod-eng): I'll prep a short customer note in #support-alerts if this stays >5m. tagging CS. :warning:
Alex (oncall): running runbook step 1: cycle connection pools on api-proxy in us-east. Command I'm running: ```for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=api-proxy -o name); do kubectl exec $p -- kill -HUP 1 || true; done```
Sanjay (infra): found db-node-3 (us-east-1) with CPU 98% and avg await high. iostat shows spikes on sda. Suspect noisy neighbor or degraded disk.
Leah (sre): can we route synthetics or read-only traffic to us-west temporarily? Avoid promoting replicas unless writes impacted.
Maya (prod-eng): agree — don't promote. I'll flip routing for synthetic canaries to us-west to stop noisy alerts while infra investigates.
incident-bot: Routing change executed: canary group 'db-conn' now served from prod-us-west-2. Synthetic checks auto-suppressed for group until further notice.
Alex (oncall): after routing change, 5xx rate trending down. Quick metric snapshot: 5xx_rate before ~1.8% -> after ~0.9%.
Leah (sre): confirmed downstream errors reduced. Peak impacted requests ~12 req/min. Looks contained to a small subset of traffic.
Sanjay (infra): initiating maintenance on db-node-3: draining replica and scheduling disk-level checks. If disk health bad, we'll replace the instance.
Alex (oncall): keeping the page open for monitoring. If stable for 30m, we'll close and create a follow-up postmortem. @Maya can you open the incident ticket and include commands + timeline?
Maya (prod-eng): creating ticket INC-9876 in Jira with timeline, affected customers, runbook steps, and the routing change. Adding logs and the commands we ran.
Leah (sre): good. Follow-ups: run storage diagnostics, check kernel IO scheduler, and review autoscaling of DB replicas.
pd-bot: PagerDuty note: escalation scheduled to SRE lead (Leah) if not resolved in +10m.
Alex (oncall): planning handoff to Leah in ~25m as I have a conflict. Leaving notes in the ticket and summary here.
Leah (sre): acknowledged handoff. I'll take over watch and trigger full maintenance if we see flapping. Great quick response team :tada:
incident-bot: This thread was automatically closed after 35 minutes of inactivity. For details see INC-9876.
